item.title: OKF MCP server
item.description: OKF (Open Knowledge Format) is Google’s spec for representing a knowledge base as a directory of linked Markdown files — YAML frontmatter for structured metadata (type, title, tags), a Markdown body for the actual content, and regular [link](path.md) references between files forming a graph. It’s a plain-text, git-friendly way to store the kind of internal knowledge that used to live in a wiki or a pile of Confluence pages, and it maps cleanly onto how an LLM wants to consume information: bounded chunks with explicit relationships, not a search index.
